note: These ARE the package defaults: an agent should apply them without asking. Every value here is measured, and the file is the single place to change a default.
kv_dtype_note: fp8 works on both arches and is the speed tier. Switch to the 4-bit capacity tier only when the context must grow: rk4v4 on 8.9, nvfp4 on 12.0 (rk4v4 is REJECTED on a 12.0 card).

spec.note: Measured on an RTX 5090 D, same binary, no rebuild: MTP d3 250-268 t/s, best MTP 343.8, DFlash2 K=7 512.9 on predictable content and 154.7 on prose. DFlash2 needs its own artifact and --lm-head-draft is mandatory (without it the engine dies with linear_topk: unsupported head profile).

ctx_note: With fp8 KV the KV term is about 32 KiB per token: 131072 costs about 4 GiB. The engine refuses a context that does not fit and prints how many bytes are missing, so a wrong value fails loudly, not silently.
engine_args_note: 1024 was swept against 128..2048 and won; it is passed explicitly so a future engine default cannot silently change it.
rung_note: 33 is our card's crossing point and is deliberately NOT lowered (on our card 17 makes T=16..31 slower and its PPL 0.025 percent worse). The crossing is a property of the CARD, so the value is exposed as an env: sweep it on one binary with `sweep`, and prove the arm ran with the probe (s8_min=). Set these explicitly at every start so the run is self-documenting.
compiled_into_the_engines_shipped_here: sm_89:  -DNINFER_CUDA_ARCH=89 (Ada tier, rk4v4 KV kernels available)
both:   int8 threshold overridable at runtime, no rebuild needed
do_not_change_without_measuring: K above 7 (a round cost of 8 or more drafts leaves the small-batch rung and the cost jumps about 3x)
context under the VRAM class above (it is a capacity limit, not a preference)
the KV dtype on a 12.0 card to rk4v4 (rejected by the engine)
